{{Short description|Italian statistician (1890–1969)}}
[[File:Marcello Boldrini.jpg|thumb|Marcello Boldrini]]
'''Marcello Boldrini''' (9 February 1890, in [[Matelica]] – 5 March 1969, in [[Milan]]) was an Italian [[statistician]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Italian Mathematics Between the Two World Wars |last=Guerraggio |first=Angelo |author2=Pietro Nastasi |page=154 |year=2006 |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |isbn=9783764375126 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Beginning in 1922, he taught courses in statistics, [[biometry]], and [[demography]] at [[Bocconi University]] of Milan, and then at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] as Emeritus Professor. He was also a member of several academies and institutes in Italy and abroad, serving for several years as president of the [[International Statistical Institute]]. His scientific research was on both methodological and applied statistics, particularly on demography, [[anthropometry]], and economics. As a statistician, he has been particularly interested in the foundations of the method, and he proposed a view of statistics as an empirical history of all the positive sciences.{{clarify|date=September 2013}} To deepen this research he founded a statistical Laboratory at the [[Catholic University of Milan]]. The results are widely discussed in the volumes, Statistica: Teoria e metodi (first edition, 1942), and Teoria della Statistica (1963), which have been studied by thousands of students. For Boldrini, Statistics is a formal science like mathematics and logic, but it is different from them as a scientific inquiry method in the inductive and deductive phases of research.

Beyond academic commitment, he also had several management positions in the state oil industry: he was first named president of [[Agip]] (1948–1953),<ref>{{cite book |title=Reappraising State-Owned Enterprise: A Comparison of the UK and Italy |authorlink=Franco Amatori |last=Amatori |first=Franco |author2=Robert Millward |author3=Pier Angelo Toninelli  |page=171 |year=2013 |publisher=[[Routledge]] |isbn=9781136738302 }}</ref> was then vice-president of [[Eni|ENI]] (1953–1962), before succeeding [[Enrico Mattei]] as president in 1962,<ref>{{cite book |title=Ente Nazionale Idrocarburi: Profile of a State Corporation |last=Dechert |first=Charles Richard |page=viii |year=1963 |publisher=[[E. J. Brill]] |oclc=6155960 }}</ref> remaining in the post until 1967.

==Academic Positions==
Professor of Statistics and Demography at the Universities of [[University of Messina|Messina]], [[University of Padua|Padua]], Milan and Rome. Dean of Political Sciences, [[Milan Catholic University]] (1043-1945).

==Honours, memberships==
Member of the [[Pontifical Academy]],{{which|date=September 2013}} [[Accademia dei Lincei]], Honoris Causa at the [[University of Rio de Janeiro]]. Professor emeritus at Rome University.

==Selected works==

===English===
* ''Scientific Truth and Statistical Method'', translated by Ruth Kendall, Griffin (1972) {{ISBN|0-8526-4197-4}}

===Italian===
* ''Biometrica'', CEDAM (1927);
* ''Demografia'', A. Giuffrè (1943);
* ''Statistica in Compendio'', A. Giuffrè (1957)
* ''Teoria della Statistica'', A. Giuffrè (1963).
* ''Statistica, Teoria e Metodi'', A. Giuffrè (5th ed. 1968)
